Question B-008-005-006.

Why the correct answer is right: An alternating-current (AC) line filter for radio-frequency (RF) noise should pass the low-frequency mains power and attenuate radio-frequency energy. That is a low-pass response.

Why the distractors are wrong:
- sourceIndex 1: "High-pass": A high-pass response would reject the wanted mains frequency and pass the unwanted RF noise, the opposite of the goal.
- sourceIndex 2: "Band-pass": A band-pass filter is not needed for ordinary power-line filtering because the wanted energy is at very low mains frequency.
- sourceIndex 3: "Band-reject": A band-reject filter removes only a selected range; an AC line RF filter needs broad attenuation of RF above the power frequency.
